title: Closed-pair restriction for a supported finite scalar local model
statement:
Let ell be prime and Lambda a commutative condensed ring isomorphic to one of the
five coefficient rings in lem-sfb-supported-three-term-scalar-rigidity: a finite discrete
commutative ring killed by an ell power, Z_ell, O_E, Q_ell, or E for a finite intermediate
extension E/Q_ell. Let t:T0→T be
a closed immersion of qcqs schemes whose restriction maps on every torsion abelian etale
sheaf are bijective in every nonnegative cohomological degree. Let p be an arbitrary path
from S to the root T in a finite qcqs open-closed tree, with quasi-compact complementary
open at each closed edge, and let J be its actual composite of open extension by zero and
closed direct image on internal Lambda modules. If N on S has a pro-etale cover on which
it is pulled back from a finitely presented Lambda-module on the point, then the actual
derived restriction RΓ(T,JN[0])→RΓ(T0,t*JN[0]) is an isomorphism in D(Ab). No assertion is
made about arbitrary images, kernels or homology of morphisms of local models.

proof.text: First prove finite-model comparison for every admissible chain rooted in $T$. For finite discrete $A$, each finite scalar local model is a locally constant finite $A$-module by the finite-discrete encoding lemma. The finite-local-system descent theorem makes it classical. Along a chain, extension by zero is still constructible: at an open arrow append the closed complementary zero stratum, and at a closed arrow append the open complementary zero stratum. Pull back the finite stratification on the image and use the restriction and vanishing identities for $a_!,a_*$; every complement involved is constructible because the specified open is quasi-compact. Thus $JL$ is constructible in the definition used by the discrete constructible-comparison theorem, so is classical. Since the finite ring is Noetherian, this theorem and the classical-module equivalence supply an étale $A$-module $F$ with $\nu_T^*F\cong JL$. Its underlying abelian sheaf is locally torsion (indeed killed by the exponent of $A$).

proof.text: Use discrete derived site comparison on $F[0]$ and on $t_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}F[0]$. The canonical pullback comparison identifies the latter's pro-étale realization with $t^*JL[0]$. These comparisons carry restriction to restriction: before deriving, both composites are the unit for restriction followed by the comparison unit; the equality is the naturality of the unit for the composite inverse-image adjunction. Derive that equality on injective resolutions. On each cohomology group the coefficient-forgetting comparison identifies the étale module restriction with the underlying abelian restriction. The hypothesis of the item makes this map bijective for every nonnegative degree; all negative groups vanish. Consequently the actual restriction is an isomorphism in $D(\mathbf{Ab})$. This proves $\mathsf B_A(t)$, meaning comparison for every supported finite scalar model, uniformly in the support chain.

proof.text: For R=Z_ell or R=O_E, apply the supported integral-model restriction-tower theorem to obtain its normalized RestrictionComparison. For each finite-level etale module F_n, ellPower makes its underlying abelian sheaf torsion. Forgetting scalars and evaluating the normalized derived sections identifies the actual restriction on every nonnegative cohomology group with ht; negative groups vanish. Exact evaluation of strict towers commutes with cohomology. Thus the homology of the tower restriction is a natural transformation whose every component is invertible; NatTrans.isIso_iff_isIso_app and DerivedCategory.isIso_iff prove invertibility of the tower restriction itself. Apply the right-derived inverse-limit functor, which preserves isomorphisms. The iso field of RestrictionComparison is an isomorphism in the arrow category from integralArrows to etaleArrows. Arrow.isIso_hom_iff_isIso_hom_of_isIso transports invertibility back to the original integral restriction. Transport along the coefficient isomorphisms to handle the stated presentations. This proves the integral single-model comparison uniformly in paths, without any assertion that arbitrary images are complete.

proof.text: Apply the rational transfer implication first to $(R,K)=(\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathbf Q_\ell)$ and then to $(\mathcal O_E,E)$ for each finite intermediate $E$. Its additional premise is the universal finite-model property proved in the previous step; the torsion-pair premise is unchanged. This yields $\mathsf B_{\mathbf Q_\ell}(t)$ and every $\mathsf B_E(t)$. Together with the finite discrete case this supplies $\mathsf B_\Lambda(t)$ for every coefficient in the item.

lean.statement:
theorem supported_finite_model_scalar_rigidity
    (Λ : Sheaf (coherentTopology Profinite.{u}) Ab.{u + 1})
    [MonObj Λ] [IsCommMonObj Λ] (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime]
    (hΛ :
      (∃ (A : Type) (_ : CommRing A) (_ : TopologicalSpace A)
          (_ : DiscreteTopology A) (_ : IsTopologicalRing A),
        Finite A ∧ (∃ n : ℕ, ∀ a : A, (ℓ ^ n) • a = 0) ∧
          Nonempty (Mon.mk Λ ≅ Mon.mk (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj A))) ∨
      Nonempty (Mon.mk Λ ≅ Mon.mk (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj ℤ_[ℓ])) ∨
      (∃ E : PadicAlgCl.FiniteIntermediateField ℓ,
        Nonempty (Mon.mk Λ ≅ Mon.mk (Profinite.padicIntegersRingObj ℓ E))) ∨
      Nonempty (Mon.mk Λ ≅ Mon.mk (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj ℚ_[ℓ])) ∨
      (∃ E : PadicAlgCl.FiniteIntermediateField ℓ,
        Nonempty (Mon.mk Λ ≅ Mon.mk (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj E))))
    {T₀ T S : Scheme.{u}} [CompactSpace T] [QuasiSeparatedSpace T]
    [CompactSpace T₀] [QuasiSeparatedSpace T₀]
    (t : T₀ ⟶ T) [IsClosedImmersion t]
    (ht : ∀ (F : Sheaf T.smallEtaleTopology Ab.{u + 1}),
      Scheme.IsTorsionAbelianSheaf F → ∀ q : ℕ,
        Function.Bijective (Etale.cohomologyMap t F q))
    (tree : QcqsOpenClosedTree T) (p : tree.Path S)
    (N : Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology S) Ab.{u + 1}) (condensedRingObj Λ S))
    (hN : HasFiniteConstantLocalModel Λ S N) :
    IsIso ((supportedModelDerivedRestriction Λ t p).app N)
